key_idea: For a target balance B, feasibility is a max-flow: source -> wire (capacity d) -> its two spheres -> sink (capacity B), feasible iff the flow is n*B; feasibility is monotone in B, so binary search.
sketch: Binary search B in [0, total/n]; for each B build the bipartite wire/sphere network and run Dinic, accepting if max flow equals n*B. Monotone because a feasible assignment for B can drop one disk per sphere. Answer is total - n*B_max. About 23 Dinic runs on 700 nodes and 1500 edges. Pitfall: a sphere of small total incident disks caps B for everyone (sample 2), and capacities should be 64-bit.
